retrieval_relevance_policy.description: A retrieved chunk is relevant when its source document matches and its zero-based loader page index is listed in relevant_sources. This keeps the ground truth stable when chunk size or overlap changes.
retrieval_relevance_policy.page_numbering: pdf_page_number is one-based for humans; loader_page_index is zero-based for PyPDFLoader-style metadata; printed_page is the page number printed in the textbook.
retrieval_relevance_policy.primary_metric_note: For questions whose answer spans several pages, use Recall@K over the listed relevant pages and Hit@K for the presence of at least one relevant page.

examples.question: What are the four strokes of a four-stroke petrol engine, and how many crankshaft revolutions complete one cycle?
examples.expected_answer: The four strokes are suction (intake), compression, expansion (power), and exhaust. One complete cycle takes two crankshaft revolutions.

examples.question: In a CRDI diesel engine, how is high-pressure fuel supplied to the injectors, and what controls injection timing and fuel quantity?
examples.expected_answer: A separate pump keeps fuel at high pressure in a shared common rail, which supplies each injector through connecting pipes. A solenoid valve at each injector regulates injection timing and fuel quantity from electronic control module inputs.
expected_answer_facts: pipes or connectors feed each injector
electronic control module controls timing and quantity

examples.question: Why must engine lubricating oil have a suitable viscosity rather than a viscosity that is very low or very high?
examples.expected_answer: Oil with very low viscosity is too thin to maintain a lubricating film between contacting surfaces. Oil with very high viscosity forms a film that itself resists motion and increases friction, so a suitable intermediate viscosity is required.
expected_answer_facts: low viscosity oil is too thin
low viscosity cannot form an adequate film

examples.question: How does a friction clutch gradually transfer rotary motion from a driving shaft to a driven shaft?
examples.expected_answer: Rough discs attached to the driving and driven shafts are pressed together. Contact creates friction, and increasing the pressure increases the frictional force, causing the driven disc and shaft to accelerate until both shafts rotate at nearly the same speed.
expected_answer_facts: rough disc surfaces are brought into contact

examples.question: What are the three main elements of the torque converter described in the textbook, and how is each connected?
examples.expected_answer: The three elements are the driving element or impeller connected to the engine shaft, the driven member or rotor connected to the driven or propeller shaft, and the fixed reaction member connected to the frame.
expected_answer_facts: rotor connected to driven or propeller shaft

examples.question: According to the textbook, what three contributions make up a vehicle's stopping distance?
examples.expected_answer: Stopping distance includes the distance traveled during the driver's reaction time, the distance traveled while the brake mechanism responds after the pedal is pressed, and the distance required to stop due to the vehicle's speed.
expected_answer_facts: distance during brake mechanism response time

examples.question: Why is a four-channel antilock braking system described as the most effective configuration, and what does the main accumulator do?
examples.expected_answer: A four-channel ABS has an independent hydraulic circuit and a separate speed sensor for each wheel, so braking can be controlled wheel by wheel. The main accumulator stores brake fluid, maintains high system pressure, and supplies pressure for power-assisted braking; nitrogen and brake fluid are separated by a diaphragm.

examples.question: What geometric condition is required for correct steering without tyre slip, and how do the inner and outer front-wheel steering angles compare?
examples.expected_answer: The axes of the two front stub axles and the rear-wheel axis must intersect at one instantaneous center of rotation. During a turn, the inner front wheel must turn through a larger angle than the outer front wheel, so theta is greater than phi.
expected_answer_facts: front stub-axle axes and rear-wheel axis intersect at one point
that point is the instantaneous center
inner wheel angle is larger than outer wheel angle

examples.question: Which operating variables are monitored by an adaptive suspension, and how are those measurements used?
examples.expected_answer: Sensors monitor vehicle height, speed, steering angle, braking force, throttle position, ignition state, damper status, and even door position. A computer analyzes these inputs and switches the suspension to the desired operating mode, using variable electronic dampers and variable-rate air springs.

examples.question: Why must a blown automotive fuse be replaced with another fuse of the same current rating?
examples.expected_answer: A lower-rated fuse may blow during normal current flow, while a higher-rated fuse may fail to interrupt an excessive current and allow other circuit components to be damaged. The replacement must therefore have the same maximum current rating.
expected_answer_facts: lower rating may blow under normal current
higher rating may not blow during excessive current
higher rating can allow component damage
replacement must use the same rating
evidence_terms: components of the circuit would be damaged
